runs.t: MNRF (Microneedling Radiofrequency)
1. Hero & Intro
MNRF Treatment for Acne Scars

The pimples went away years ago. The pits they left behind didn't. Acne scars are stubborn because they're not a surface problem, they're a dip in the skin where collagen got damaged, and no cream is going to fill that back in. If you've been reading up on MNRF treatment for acne scars in Delhi, you've probably reached that conclusion already.

MNRF, short for microneedling radiofrequency, works deeper than a regular facial or peel. Tiny insulated needles carry radiofrequency heat under the skin's surface, where scar tissue sits. The skin responds by building fresh collagen, and over a course of sessions the dents start to look shallower and the texture smoother. It's also used for stretch marks and large pores.
Available at Dadu Medical Centre Vasant Vihar (South Delhi) & Rajouri Garden (West Delhi), under Dr. Nivedita Dadu.
2. How MNRF Works

The needles are insulated along their length, so the radiofrequency energy comes out at the tips, below the epidermis. That's where the scar tissue and collagen fibres are. The outer layer of skin gets very little of the heat, which is why the surface heals quickly.

Two things happen at once. The tiny needle punctures switch on the skin's own healing response and release growth factors. The RF pulse then heats the deeper tissue, breaking down the old, tight collagen bands and prompting fibroblasts to lay down new collagen. Put together, that's a stronger push for repair than needling or heat would give on their own.
After your consultation, the dermatologist decides whether MNRF on its own is enough or whether it should be followed by Collagen Induction Therapy, depending on your scars.
3. MNRF vs Regular Microneedling

People often ask about this. Regular microneedling uses needles alone, which creates small controlled injuries that nudge collagen production. MNRF adds radiofrequency heat through those same needles, so the effect reaches deeper and tends to be stronger, which matters for pitted acne scars.
4. What MNRF Can Help With
Acne scars

are the main reason people book it, particularly the depressed, pitted kind left by cystic or deep inflamed acne. As old scar tissue breaks down and new collagen fills in, those dips gradually look shallower.
Stretch marks
from pregnancy, weight changes or growth spurts can also soften in texture and colour.
Large pores
often look tighter as the collagen around them rebuilds, and skin that's dull or uneven usually looks smoother overall.
5. Benefits Section

The biggest difference compared with creams and peels is depth. MNRF reaches the layer where scars actually sit, and it uses heat plus needling to rebuild that layer rather than just polishing the surface. Because the energy goes in below the epidermis, downtime is short, usually a day or two of redness. And since surface pigment isn't heavily targeted, it's considered a good option for darker skin, which tends to be prone to marks after more aggressive treatments.
6. Ideal Candidates

MNRF is a good fit if you have pitted or uneven acne scars, stretch marks you'd like to soften, or enlarged pores that make skin look rough. It's often recommended for Indian and darker skin tones for the reasons above. The dermatologist will look at how deep and severe the scars are before planning sessions.
7. Process & Techniques

It starts with a consultation, where the dermatologist assesses your scars or stretch marks and decides on MNRF alone or MNRF followed by Collagen Induction Therapy. On the day, a numbing cream is applied first. Once it's taken effect, the MNRF handpiece is moved over the area. Most people describe a mild warmth or tingling rather than pain.
How many sessions?

For acne scars, most people need six to eight sessions, three to four weeks apart. Deeper or more severe scarring can take longer. Texture usually starts to look better after two or three sessions, and the bigger change builds as the course goes on. Results vary from person to person.
Recovery:
Expect some redness, a bit like mild sunburn, for one to two days. There's no significant downtime, and most people are back to their normal routine within a day or two.

10. FAQs
Q: How much does MNRF cost in Delhi?
Ans. Roughly ₹6,000 to ₹10,000 a session. Your exact cost depends on the treatment plan and is confirmed at consultation.
Q: How many sessions do acne scars need?
Ans. Usually six to eight, spaced three to four weeks apart. Deeper scars can take a bit more.
Q: Is MNRF painful?
Ans. Numbing cream goes on first, so most people only feel warmth or tingling while it's being done.
Q: What's the difference between microneedling and MNRF?
Ans. Microneedling uses needles alone. MNRF sends radiofrequency heat through the needles, which reaches deeper and gives a stronger collagen boost.
Q: How long is the downtime?
Ans. Your skin may look red, a bit like mild sunburn, for a day or two. Most people get back to normal by the next day.
Q: Is it safe for dark skin?
Ans. It's considered a good option, because the energy is delivered under the surface rather than to surface pigment.
Q: When will I see a difference?
Ans. Texture usually starts looking better after two or three sessions, with more change as the course goes on.
Q: Does MNRF help stretch marks too?
Ans. Yes. It can soften their texture and colour, and the doctor will plan sessions after seeing them.
